decision_procedure: 1. Establish the safety envelope and fix requirements before building any layer: for electronics/automation set electrical/power/battery safety limits, fusing, isolation, and (for automation) the fail-safe/safe-state envelope; for self-hosting fix scope, named users, capacity targets, data-sensitivity, and budget/power constraints. Safety and requirements dominate convenience and speed and gate everything downstream.

2. Route by subdomain: a 'design/bring up a circuit or embedded board (sensors, actuators, buses, power, firmware, PWM/ADC)' need -> the electronics & microcontrollers track; a 'plan/operate a home server or self-hosted service (storage, OS, containers, network, backups, security, ops)' need -> the home servers & self-hosting track; a 'automate the physical world (IoT/MQTT, automation rules, robotics, feedback, fail-safe)' need -> the physical computing & automation track. Many maker projects chain electronics build -> firmware/automation -> optional self-hosted hub/services, in dependency order.

3. For electronics & microcontrollers, execute in dependency order: safety/power limits -> Ohm's-law operating points and topology -> datasheet-grounded component selection -> schematic capture and breadboard prototype -> regulated power and MCU/board selection (fix 3.3V/5V domain) -> GPIO config and non-blocking firmware -> ADC input and PWM output -> buses/sensors/actuators/connectivity -> incremental bring-up and measured debug, soldering only verified circuits -> integrate verified subsystems and run final safety/acceptance tests.

4. For home servers & self-hosting, execute in dependency order: scope/capacity and hardware -> storage redundancy and hardened base OS -> stable addressing/names, segmentation, and default-deny firewall -> container runtime, app deployment with persistent volumes/pinned tags, and safe secret injection -> reverse-proxy TLS and authentication/authorization -> VPN remote access with deliberate hardened public exposure -> 3-2-1 backups, proven restore, and UPS -> monitoring/alerting and a reversible patch cadence -> reconcile a hardening baseline and capture config/runbooks -> periodic capacity/aging/lifecycle review.

5. For physical computing & automation, execute in dependency order: sense-decide-act requirements and BOM -> power/fusing/isolation/SELV and environmental safety envelope -> platform and firmware architecture matched to timing/I/O -> sensor interfacing, actuator/motor drive, and reliable wiring -> links/messaging/hub state model -> triggers/rules and closed sensor->actuator feedback loops -> safe states/interlocks/watchdogs and device/network hardening -> bench/fault-injection/HIL validation plus telemetry and OTA path -> on-site commissioning -> operate/monitor/maintain.

6. Drive loads correctly and protect parts: never drive a load above the pin current limit directly from a logic pin (use a rated driver stage); always add a flyback/snubber on inductive loads; keep actuator inrush off the logic rail with a separate/decoupled rail; never mix 3.3V/5V domains without explicit level shifting; size every device rating above worst-case and check power dissipation and units.

7. Ground claims and measure, do not guess: take ratings, pinouts, and bus addresses from the official datasheet over forum/AI lore; localize faults with measured per-net values rather than guess-and-swap; verify a subsystem before integrating or enclosing it and before soldering a not-yet-proven circuit.

8. Protect data and exposure in self-hosting: an off-box versioned backup is mandatory and never substituted by RAID; a backup is not proven until a restore is tested against RTO/RPO; enforce default-deny and segmentation, account for Docker published ports bypassing the host firewall, prefer VPN over public exposure, allow public ingress only with hardening plus a decision record, and keep secrets out of git/container layers with least-privilege MFA identity.

9. Keep control local and fail-safe in automation: safety interlocks, watchdogs, and e-stop always override convenience automation and any cloud link; manual override and e-stop win over autonomous rules; OTA updates must be validated, signed, staged, and reversible and must preserve safe states; delegate PID design, stability margins, and oscillation/hysteresis analysis of closed sensor->actuator loops to the feedback-loops specialist.

10. Apply dominance rules at every conflict: safety/fail-safe > speed; dependency order > value order; risk/irreversibility > delivery speed; datasheet authority > forum lore; measured evidence > guess-and-swap; rated driver/separate rail > direct pin drive/shared rail; non-blocking timing > blocking simplicity; subsystem verification > integration speed; off-box backup > RAID; proven restore > assumed backup; default-deny/security > public exposure/ease; VPN > broad exposure; least-privilege > convenience; local safe control > cloud dependence; safety-rated parts > cost; human review > automation for irreversible/high-risk steps; acceptance testing/QA > early lock.

11. Validate and ground before lock: run the relevant acceptance/safety tests (power within limits and fused, short-check passed, every inductive load protected, default-deny enforced and IoT/guest cannot reach the management plane, restore validated, safe-state reached on fault injection); label all numeric values heuristic unless eligible observed/experimental data exists (observed_impact and data_quality stay 0.0 absent data); attach each recommendation to a competency question and an authoritative source; and route high-risk/irreversible nodes (first power-up/mains/lithium, new inductive driver, soldering/irreversible assembly, final close, RAID/storage layout, secrets, backups, restore/DR, public exposure, security hardening, fail-safe, feedback control, OTA, deployment) to human review.

escalation_triggers.condition: any mains/AC or above-SELV (e.g., >24V) involvement, a battery chemistry change, or a high-current actuator added, where the build approaches the licensed-mains / high-voltage exclusion boundary
escalation_triggers.reason: mains and high-voltage work is out of scope and a fire/shock hazard; it must be reviewed and may need a licensed professional

escalation_triggers.condition: a self-hosting irreversible or data-loss-risking decision: storage/RAID layout, secrets management, backup strategy, restore/DR testing, or security hardening baseline
escalation_triggers.reason: these nodes are flagged human_review_required and carry irreversible data-integrity or security consequences

escalation_triggers.condition: a service is to be exposed to the public internet, or a port-forward/public ingress is proposed
escalation_triggers.reason: public exposure changes the deliberate attack surface; default-deny and hardening dominate and the exposure needs a decision record and review

escalation_triggers.condition: an automation node informs an irreversible/hazardous physical action: fail-safe/safe-state design, power/electrical safety, feedback control of real hardware, device security, OTA update, or on-site deployment/commissioning
escalation_triggers.reason: fault energy, actuator motion, and exposed updates can cause physical harm or fleet-wide failure and require sign-off before lock

escalation_triggers.condition: a closed sensor->actuator loop needs PID design, stability/margin certification, or oscillation/limit-cycle/hysteresis analysis
escalation_triggers.reason: tie closed-loop control to the feedback-loops specialist; do not assert stability or tuning without that analysis

escalation_triggers.condition: a critical rating, pinout, or bus address would be taken from a forum/AI snippet against (or absent) the official datasheet, or a part choice is unsupported
escalation_triggers.reason: datasheet authority dominates forum lore for ratings/pinouts/addresses; resolve grounding before committing the part

escalation_triggers.condition: a hard lock/close/deploy is requested before acceptance/safety tests (electronics), before a proven restore (self-hosting), or before fault-injection/HIL validation and a confirmed safe state (automation) pass
escalation_triggers.reason: acceptance testing and QA dominate locking; run scoped validation first

escalation_triggers.condition: a load above the pin current limit would be driven directly from a logic pin, an inductive load lacks a flyback/snubber, actuator inrush would share the logic rail, or 3.3V/5V domains would be mixed without level shifting
escalation_triggers.reason: direct pin drive, missing flyback, shared inrush rail, and unshifted cross-domain signals destroy parts or brown out the MCU

escalation_triggers.condition: RAID is offered as a backup substitute, password SSH or a shared admin account is left enabled, secrets are stored in a container layer or git, an image is unpinned (:latest), or a Docker published port bypasses the host firewall
escalation_triggers.reason: these are known self-hosting failure modes that silently undermine recovery, access control, and the firewall posture

escalation_triggers.condition: a numeric value (current/voltage/power, capacity, RTO/RPO, margin, threshold, timing) is presented as observed or experimentally validated without eligible supplied data, or observed_impact/data_quality are nonzero absent a dataset
escalation_triggers.reason: evidence-label correctness dominates numeric precision; relabel as heuristic

validation_checklist: Electrical/power/battery safety is set before any hands-on or powered step: the source is within rated limits and fused, a short-circuit check passed before power, lithium cells are handled per chemistry rules, and any mains/above-SELV/chemistry change is flagged out-of-scope or for human review.
Every DC node is computed with V=IR/P=VI in consistent units with power dissipation checked per resistor, and each passive and semiconductor's value/tolerance/rating exceeds its worst-case role.

Every inductive load has a flyback/snubber, no load above the pin current limit is driven directly from a logic pin, actuator inrush is kept off the logic rail (separate/decoupled rail), and 3.3V/5V cross-domain signals are explicitly level-shifted.

The schematic labels every net/component with explicit power and ground, the breadboard has no high-current paths, soldered joints are shiny/sound with no bridges and continuity verified, and a circuit is soldered only after it is proven on breadboard.

Faults are localized by comparing measured vs expected values per net with a correctly-ranged multimeter (right jack/mode) rather than guess-and-swap, and each subsystem is verified before it is integrated or enclosed.

Power rails are sized and regulated with adequate dropout/current/thermal headroom and decoupling at supply and IC pins, the board logic-voltage domain is fixed, and critical ratings/pinouts/bus-addresses are taken from the official datasheet.
Self-hosting requirements name every planned service and user with numeric, testable capacity targets, and the chosen hardware platform meets them within the power/thermal/budget/noise constraints.

The storage/RAID level survives the documented disk-failure tolerance with scrub/resilver clean and usable capacity met after overhead, RAID is never treated as a backup, a 3-2-1 versioned off-box backup exists, and a restore has been proven against measured RTO/RPO with a DR runbook; UPS + graceful shutdown protect active writes.

The base OS uses key-only SSH (PasswordAuthentication disabled), a non-root admin user, and NTP; the container runtime decision (rootless/rootful) is made; apps run with persistent volumes, pinned (non-:latest) image tags, resource limits, and injected secrets, with no data in an ephemeral container layer.

Addressing uses static IP/DHCP reservations with local DNS; a default-deny host firewall plus VLAN/subnet segmentation isolates IoT/guest from the management plane and accounts for Docker published ports bypassing the host firewall; the reverse proxy terminates TLS via ACME with HTTP->HTTPS redirect and correct per-host routing.

Remote access uses a VPN (WireGuard/Tailscale) by default; any public ingress is a deliberate, hardened decision with a record and exposed-surface inventory; secrets live in a real store (not git/container layers) with rotation; identity is least-privilege with per-user MFA/SSO; a hardening baseline, monitoring/alerting, a reversible patch cadence, runbooks, and a lifecycle/capacity review are in place.

Automation requirements list every sense->decide->act triple with measurable thresholds and an environment class, a feasible BOM, and a platform/firmware architecture matched to real-time/I/O needs with a non-blocking task/loop structure.

Sensors are interfaced with correct logic levels, pull-ups, and calibration producing trustworthy readings; actuators/motors are driven through rated, protected drivers within peak/stall current limits; MQTT topics/QoS/retain/LWT and the hub entity/state model are defined; and automation rules/schedules have a coherent precedence map.

Every fault, hang, or sensor loss drives a defined safe state via watchdog/interlock/e-stop with an actuator power-removal means; manual override and e-stop win over autonomous rules; safety-relevant and core control work locally without a cloud link; and closed-loop PID/stability/oscillation analysis is delegated to the feedback-loops specialist.

Behavior is validated by bench/fault-injection/HIL with a deployment go/no-go and a confirmed safe state before controlling real hardware; OTA updates are signed, versioned, staged, and reversible and preserve safe states; observability/telemetry and a maintenance/calibration/EOL plan exist.

All acceptance/safety tests for the relevant subdomain pass before any hard lock/close/deploy, and high-risk/irreversible nodes (first power-up/mains/lithium, new inductive driver, soldering/irreversible assembly, final close, RAID/storage, secrets, backups, restore/DR, public exposure, security hardening, fail-safe, feedback control, OTA, deployment) are human-reviewed with a decision record.

Every numeric value (current/voltage/power, capacity, RTO/RPO, margins, thresholds, timing) is labeled heuristic unless eligible observed/experimental data exists (observed_impact and data_quality remain 0.0 absent data), and each recommendation/claim traces to a competency question and at least one authoritative source (Platt; Monk; Banzi & Shiloh; Upton & Halfacree; Nemeth et al.; datasheets).

conflicts_and_dominance.tradeoff: electrical/power safety and fail-safe vs build speed/convenience
conflicts_and_dominance.resolution: electrical/power/battery safety and fail-safe/safe-state behavior dominate speed and convenience for any power source above coin-cell, any inductive/actuator load, or any hazard; complete fusing/short-check/staged power-up and interlocks before proceeding (override requires a recorded risk acceptance).

conflicts_and_dominance.tradeoff: dependency order vs perceived value order
conflicts_and_dominance.resolution: true dependency precedence dominates raw value ordering; finish prerequisites (safety/requirements -> foundations/platform -> I/O/services -> integration -> validation) before sequencing a higher-value node that depends on them.
data-integrity and irreversibility risk (storage layout, soldering, secrets, public exposure, actuator deployment) dominate delivery speed; slow down and route to human review where flagged.
the official datasheet dominates forum/AI snippets for ratings, pinouts, and bus addresses; ground critical specs in the datasheet before committing the part.
measured per-net evidence dominates guess-and-swap for any non-trivial fault; measure with a correctly-ranged meter and compare expected vs measured before swapping parts.

conflicts_and_dominance.tradeoff: rated driver stage / separate rail vs direct pin drive / shared rail
conflicts_and_dominance.resolution: a rated driver stage dominates direct pin drive for any load above the pin current limit, and separate/decoupled actuator power dominates a single shared rail whenever motor inrush can brown out the logic; always add flyback/snubber on inductive loads.
non-blocking timing dominates blocking simplicity on any path with PWM, bus, input-timing, or a control-loop deadline; restructure firmware rather than insert blocking delays.

conflicts_and_dominance.tradeoff: subsystem verification / breadboard reversibility vs integration/solder speed
conflicts_and_dominance.resolution: bring-up verification dominates integration speed and solder durability; do not integrate, enclose, or solder a subsystem that is not yet proven on breadboard and measured.
an off-box versioned backup is mandatory and never substituted by RAID; redundancy only improves availability, and a backup is not proven until a restore is tested against RTO/RPO.

conflicts_and_dominance.tradeoff: default-deny security vs public exposure / ease of setup
conflicts_and_dominance.resolution: default-deny and segmentation plus hardening dominate; public exposure is allowed only with a documented need, hardening, and a decision record, and any path beyond the trusted segment is authenticated and encrypted before connection.

conflicts_and_dominance.tradeoff: private VPN tunnel vs frictionless public access
conflicts_and_dominance.resolution: VPN dominates for admin and sensitive data; hardened public ingress is allowed only for low-risk, deliberately-exposed services, never for the management plane.
least-privilege per-user accounts and MFA dominate the convenience of a shared admin account; keep secrets out of git/container layers with rotation.

security patches for exposed/high-severity items dominate uptime and are applied promptly with a rollback path; cosmetic updates defer, and irreversible/exposure-changing updates require human review; OTA fleet updates must be validated, signed, staged, and reversible.

conflicts_and_dominance.tradeoff: local safe control vs cloud dependence
conflicts_and_dominance.resolution: safety-relevant and core control must work locally and dominate any cloud link; cloud/OTA is for convenience only and must never sit on a safety-critical path.
manual override and e-stop always win over autonomous rules; safety interlocks and safe states override convenience automation.
safety- and rating-critical parts must meet spec regardless of cost; only non-critical parts may be cost-optimized.

conflicts_and_dominance.tradeoff: centralization (proxy/DNS/identity) vs single point of failure
conflicts_and_dominance.resolution: centralize for manageability but add a documented fallback for any component (reverse proxy, local DNS resolver, ACME renewal) whose outage takes down many services.

conflicts_and_dominance.tradeoff: feature/service ambition vs power and maintenance budget
conflicts_and_dominance.resolution: the achievable power/safety budget and ongoing patch/backup/monitor cost dominate feature ambition; add a service or feature only when its value exceeds its lifecycle cost and it fits the rail/safety budget.
QA dominates; block any hard lock, enclosure close, or deploy until acceptance/safety tests (electronics), a proven restore (self-hosting), and fault-injection/safe-state checks (automation) pass.
label correctness dominates; keep currents, voltages, capacities, RTO/RPO, margins, and timings heuristic and hold observed/experimental fields at 0.0 absent eligible data.

human review dominates automated acceptance for irreversible or high-risk nodes (first power-up/mains/lithium, new inductive driver, soldering, final close, RAID/storage, secrets, backups, restore/DR, public exposure, security hardening, fail-safe, feedback control, OTA, deployment), with a decision record.

glossary.definition: the core DC relations linking voltage, current, resistance, and power used to size every component before selection; distinct from AC impedance and phasor analysis.
a capacitor (e.g., 100nF) placed at an IC power pin to supply transient current and quiet the rail; distinct from a bulk filter capacitor alone.
a clamp across an inductive load (relay/solenoid/motor) that absorbs back-EMF when current is switched off, protecting the driver; mandatory on inductive loads, distinct from a rectifier diode role.
a transistor/MOSFET/H-bridge/IC between a logic pin and a real load that carries the load current; required whenever the load exceeds the pin current limit, distinct from direct pin drive.
the nominal logic-level family of a board/part; cross-domain signals must be explicitly level-shifted, distinct from the supply-rail voltage alone.

a GPIO is a configurable digital pin within current/voltage limits; PWM encodes a proportional value in duty cycle for dimming/speed/servo; ADC reads an analog signal into calibrated counts; PWM is not true analog output.

serial peripheral buses: I2C is a two-wire addressable bus needing pull-ups, SPI is a faster chip-select bus, UART is a point-to-point async link; each needs matching logic levels and an address/CS map.
an MCU reset or malfunction caused by the supply rail dipping below a minimum voltage, often from actuator inrush on a shared rail; prevented by a separate/decoupled rail and adequate supply margin.
the manufacturer document giving a part's ratings, pinout, and recommended circuits; the authoritative source for ratings/pinouts/addresses over forum/AI lore.

combining disks for redundancy or performance so the array survives a bounded number of failures, with checksumming filesystems (ZFS/btrfs) and periodic scrubs detecting silent corruption; RAID is redundancy, never a backup.
three copies of data on two media types with one off-site (and versioned); the mandatory data-protection standard that RAID does not satisfy, distinct from redundancy.
recovery time objective and recovery point objective: how fast recovery must complete and to what data freshness; validated by an actual restore test, distinct from an uptime SLA.

an isolated, reproducible OCI/Docker package of an app and its dependencies; persistent volumes hold data outside the ephemeral container layer so it survives recreation, distinct from a virtual machine.

a server (Nginx/Caddy/Traefik) terminating TLS and routing inbound requests by hostname; ACME automates issuing/renewing TLS certificates; a single entrypoint and high-value target, distinct from a VPN.

a firewall posture blocking all inbound except explicitly allowed flows, combined with splitting the LAN into isolated segments so a compromised IoT/guest device cannot reach the management plane; note Docker published ports can bypass the host firewall.

a VPN is an encrypted tunnel letting authenticated remote clients reach internal services without public exposure; a port-forward maps a public WAN port to an internal host, exposing it; VPN is preferred for admin/sensitive access.
an orderly automated shutdown on power loss that flushes writes and exports pools to avoid corruption; distinct from a hard power-off.
storing credentials in a real store with rotation and an injection mechanism (never in git/container layers), with per-user least-privilege accounts and multi-factor/SSO authentication.

a lightweight publish/subscribe protocol for device state and commands using a topic hierarchy, quality-of-service levels, retained messages, and a last-will-and-testament; distinct from HTTP REST or raw TCP.

a control structure where a sensor reading drives an actuator toward a setpoint; PID/stability/oscillation analysis is delegated to the feedback-loops specialist, distinct from an open-loop one-shot rule.
a deadband around a setpoint that prevents an on/off controller from chattering; distinct from PID gain.
the property that any fault, hang, or sensor loss drives the system to a defined non-harmful state (e.g., actuators de-energized); distinct from fault tolerance or high availability.

a watchdog timer resets or safe-states the device if firmware fails to service it; interlocks and an emergency-stop provide an actuator power-removal means and manual override that wins over autonomous rules.
a bounded low-voltage domain isolated from mains; the in-scope safety boundary, with mains/AC wiring and high-voltage work excluded as out-of-scope.
remote firmware update delivered over the network with versioning, signing, staging, and rollback that must preserve safe states; distinct from a manual reflash.

basic geometry mapping motion intent to actuator commands (e.g., wheel/joint geometry, differential-drive equations turning a heading into left/right wheel speeds) with encoder feedback; excludes full SLAM/path planning.

competency_questions_covered: Before any hands-on work, what electrical, power, and battery safety rules, fusing, and current/voltage limits apply, and what is the power budget?
How are voltage, current, resistance, and power computed for a DC node, and how are passives and semiconductors (with flyback/protection and ratings) selected for a role under load?
How is a circuit captured as a labeled schematic, prototyped on a breadboard, soldered reliably, and debugged by measuring expected vs actual per net with a multimeter?
How is clean, sized, regulated power provided and budgeted, and which microcontroller/SBC board and 3.3V/5V logic domain fit the I/O, connectivity, and power needs?
How are GPIO pins configured (with level shifting and drive limits) and non-blocking firmware written to read ADC analog input and emit proportional PWM safely?
How are sensors and actuators selected, driven through rated protected drivers on a separate rail, validated, and connected over I2C/SPI/UART and wireless/IoT links?
What should a home server do, for which users, under what budget/power/uptime constraints, and what hardware platform and base OS fit those numeric capacity targets?
What storage layout and RAID/ZFS level protect the data, how is data backed up off-box (3-2-1) beyond redundancy, and how is recovery proven against RTO/RPO with UPS power resilience?
How are self-hosted apps deployed reproducibly in containers with persistent volumes and pinned tags, and reached over a TLS-terminating reverse proxy?
How are addressing, local DNS, default-deny firewall, and VLAN segmentation set so only intended services are reachable and IoT/guest cannot reach the management plane (including Docker port bypass)?

How is remote access provided securely via VPN, when is public exposure justified and hardened, and how are secrets, least-privilege identity, MFA, hardening, monitoring, patching, runbooks, and lifecycle review managed?
What does an automation project need to sense, decide, and actuate within budget, on what platform and firmware architecture, and within what safety/enclosure envelope?

How are sensors read and actuators/motors driven reliably, how do devices connect and message over WiFi/BLE and MQTT, how is hub state modeled, and how are automation rules and feedback loops authored?

What guarantees the system reaches a safe state on any fault, hang, or sensor loss (watchdog/interlock/e-stop/manual override), and when is closed-loop control delegated to the feedback-loops specialist?

How are device security, signed OTA updates, observability, bench/fault-injection/HIL validation, commissioning, and lifecycle maintenance handled, and what acceptance criteria mark the build safe and working before lock?
